title: Calvo Fairies, Technology Shocks, and the Hand-to-Mouth Multiplier: New Keynesian DSGE vs. Real Business Cycle & Monetarist Macroeconomics — Stagflation, the 2008 Lehman crash & the 2021-2024 inflation surge; Lucas's 1976 policy-invariance critique & Kydland-Prescott's 1982 RBC technology-shock equilibrium; Romer & Romer's 1989/2023 narrative FOMC proof of monetary non-neutrality; Smets & Wouters's 2007 Bayesian RANK DSGE vs Paul Romer & Blanchard's hysteresis/realism indictment; Kaplan, Moll & Violante's HANK 19%-direct vs 81%-indirect revolution & Alves's fiscal propagation; USD 1,000 stimulus & -100 bps multiplier math, administrative bank-panel power & spotting macro models in disguise

teenKit.tldr: If money is just a made-up measurement tool like inches or centimeters, why does changing interest rates or mailing stimulus checks throw millions of people out of work or spark massive inflation? This episode dives into the epic 90-year intellectual war to figure out how a nominal accounting yardstick actually moves the physical world.
teenKit.whyItMatters: Understanding how macroeconomic models work determines whether governments can stop devastating recessions and control runaway inflation before it destroys people's life savings.
keyTakeaways: Nominal rigidity and sticky prices mean that changing the money supply temporarily tricks businesses and workers, altering real physical output instead of just changing prices instantly.

Traditional Representative Agent (RANK) models assumed everyone behaved like an average consumer, but they completely missed the 2008 financial crisis because they ignored how wealth inequality changes economic shocks.

The newer HANK (Heterogeneous-Agent New Keynesian) models prove that over 80% of monetary policy impact comes from indirect labor-income and cash-flow effects hitting hand-to-mouth households rather than direct savings choices.

vocab.meaning: The classic economic idea that changing a monetary unit of measurement should only change price tags, leaving real factories, jobs, and goods completely untouched.
Dynamic Stochastic General Equilibrium models are massive computer simulations used by central banks to forecast how an entire economy reacts to shocks and policy changes over time.
A modern economic framework that tracks different types of households—especially those living paycheck-to-paycheck—to see how monetary policy actually ripples through society.
Robert Lucas's famous warning that you cannot safely use historical economic data to predict the results of a new policy because people instantly change their behavior when the rules change.

quiz.question: Why does the podcast compare changing a central bank interest rate to a Bureau of Weights and Measures changing the definition of an inch?
options: To prove that central banks physically manufacture building supplies like lumber.
To highlight the mind-bending paradox that a purely nominal yardstick somehow moves real-world factories and jobs.
To show that inflation is caused entirely by carpenters building too many houses.
To argue that government regulators should control the exact length of a centimeter.
quiz.explanation: Changing a measurement unit shouldn't change physical reality, making it a profound mystery why interest rate tweaks actually cause real-world recessions or booms.

quiz.question: What was the core flaw of traditional RANK (Representative-Agent New Keynesian) macroeconomic models exposed by the 2008 financial crash?
options: They assumed every single person in the economy had identical wealth and spent money the exact same way, erasing inequality and debt friction.
They relied entirely on physical weather forecasts instead of banking data.
They refused to use computers and calculated everything by hand on paper.
They predicted the 2008 crash too early, causing panic.
quiz.explanation: Representative agent models averaged out the entire population into one single person, missing how debt and hand-to-mouth households amplify financial panics.

quiz.question: According to modern HANK research by Kaplan, Moll, and Violante, how do interest rate cuts actually drive most of the economy?
options: By convincing wealthy people to save slightly less through direct intertemporal substitution.
By magically printing physical steel mills and software engineering offices.
Through indirect labor-income and cash-flow boosts that hit cash-strapped, hand-to-mouth households who immediately spend the money.
By changing the literal definition of a metric inch.
quiz.explanation: HANK models reveal that over 80% of monetary policy power flows through indirect employment and income effects on households with little to no financial wealth.
